title: Wrap, fasten and set down a folded umbrella
instruction: Wrap the loose tie around the folded umbrella, press it closed and lay the fastened umbrella on the table.
context: Umbrellas are everyday carry: US consumption of umbrellas and walking sticks was about 142 million units in 2024 (IndexBox market overview, August 2025). A collapsed umbrella springs loose in a bag unless its tie is wrapped and fastened. The difficulty is physical: the gathered canopy springs back from about 75 mm to its 99 mm loose diameter as soon as it is let go, so it must stay gathered while the tie is wound, and the 24 mm wide hook patch must land aligned on the loop patch, no more than about 10 mm off-centre sideways, and be pressed closed. Any way of wrapping that leaves it gathered, fastened and holding after release counts.
setup: Two YAM arms, an ordinary flat table and a folded compact manual umbrella; the handle starts in the left gripper and the right gripper starts open about 60 mm from the hanging tie. Simulated sizes, with the real example in brackets (ShedRain Mini Manual Compact Umbrella, black, $15.99 at Target, 23 Nov 2026): length ferrule to handle end about 300 mm with 190 mm of folded canopy (real: listing says folds to 7 in, 178 mm, and overall length 12.01 in, 305 mm); mass 0.19 kg with the tie (real: ship weight 0.463 lb, 0.21 kg); canopy of folded fabric, loose shaft-centred diameter about 99 mm (real: recycled PET fabric, 38 in span); a 24 mm steel core for the shaft and folded ribs (real: telescoping shaft); tie 239 × 24 mm webbing with nylon hook-and-loop tape, 55 mm hook on the free end and 72 mm loop near the seam on opposite faces (real: hook-and-loop tie, sizes not listed; measure it, and fit the simulated tie if the stock one is shorter or its patches smaller). Tape marks at the strap seam and tip and a dot on the shaft end; an end-on phone with a ruler and a protractor centred on the dot, and a side phone with a standing ruler.
scoring: End-state score; how the tie is wound and which hand acts are not scored. 0.25: canopy gathered to ≤80% of its loose shaft-centred diameter (end-on photo, ruler) while held in a gripper or resting on the table. 0.50: also the tie ≥270° round the shaft (end-on photo through the protractor: tip tape at or past the three-quarter line from the seam tape). 0.75: also ≥365° round with visible overlap (tip tape at least 5° past the seam tape; second photo from the other side shows the strap continuous over the seam) and the hook patch engaged on the loop patch (photo). 1.00: also lowered onto the table, not dropped (it rests on the table before the last gripper opens; side video), both grippers ≥20 mm clear and not touching it, and once released the wrap stays gathered, wound and fastened with nothing moving for 1 s, still so at the end. Otherwise 0.
reset_notes: Simulation: the preheld handle and freely hanging strap settle under gravity before the episode. Real trials, about 2 minutes: 1) peel the hook patch fully off and unwind the tie; 2) hold the handle with the canopy down and shake gently three times so the folds hang loose, frame still collapsed; 3) pick lint off both fastener faces; 4) measure the loose shaft-centred diameter end-on: within ±5 mm of the reference taken before the first trial (about 99 mm in the model), otherwise shake and re-measure; 5) put the handle in the left gripper, seam up, tie hanging, and open the right gripper about 60 mm from the tie.
fidelity: Twelve sprung canopy and fifteen hinged strap sections approximate the fabric; constants uncalibrated. Hook-and-loop engages when aligned, overlapping patches are pressed at ≥0.15 N for three controls, in sim only by a gripper fingertip at the strap end or hook patch (real trials accept any press). Standard test closures are far heavier (18–24 N), so engaging is much easier than real. The real example folds to 178 mm (190 mm canopy here) and lists no tie sizes. The demo never reads scores.
